title: Passed Pawns
description: A passed pawn has no enemy pawns blocking or able to capture it on its way to promotion. Learn to create, support, and push passed pawns — and to blockade the opponent's.

sections.title: The Outside Passed Pawn
sections.content: An outside passed pawn — far from the other pawns — is a decisive endgame asset. It lures the enemy king away, letting your king feast on the other wing.

positions.commentary: The a-pawn is an outside passer. Pushed at the right moment, it drags the black king to the queenside while White's king invades the kingside.
hints: Use the passer as a decoy
March your king while the pawn distracts

sections.title: The Protected Passed Pawn
sections.content: A passed pawn defended by another pawn is "protected" — the enemy king cannot win it and is tied down forever. This is often a winning advantage by itself.

positions.commentary: White's e3 pawn protects the passed d4 pawn. The black king can never capture it, and White's king is free to advance.
hints: The protected passer ties the enemy down

exercises.title: Activate the King
exercises.description: White to play. Begin marching the king toward the action while the outside passer ties Black down.
hints: The king is the key piece in the endgame
